newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Tuesday were widespread at $63.00 per cwt, but passed by owners asking $65.00, several feedlot sources said.
"Everybody's bidding $63.00, but they're not acting like they want to buy cattle today," a Kansas source said.
Packers reportedly had adequate live inventories following last week's moderately active trade at $64.00 and continued to pick up cattle sold last week, cattle feeders said.
"I've probably shipped about two-thirds of what we sold last week," a southwest Kansas feedlot manager said.
Owners continued to price cattle at $65.00 amid optimism for ongoing firm beef prices, the sources said.
"Beef was up on Monday, which looks positive, but the question will be if it can stay up," one cattle feeder said.
Beef prices were quoted up $0.24 to $0.53 per cwt by USDA, compared with Friday, with 120 fabricated beef loads sold.

Gains were tied to fill-in buying by retailers following strong demand over the weekend, market sources said. Lower prices on Friday fueled talk that retailers were close to being finished stocking up for Independence Day.
